item.title: Bentonville Daily — August 9, 2026
item.description:
A Heat Advisory through Sunday night, meetings on August 11 and August 25, and a Rogers City Council meeting on August 11 are the top local happenings today.
Heat Advisory in effect through Sunday evening. A Heat Advisory is in effect for Benton and Southern Sebastian counties in Arkansas through Sunday evening, with heat index values up to 108 expected. Health officials warn of heat-related illnesses.
On the Bentonville City Council agenda: Approve a Planned Unit Development for properties at 902, 904, 906, 908, and 1002 SE 3rd Street. If approved, this PUD amendment would allow a specific development pattern on those parcels at the listed address, as recommended by the Planning Commission.
On the Bentonville Finance Committee agenda: Council to accept a grant for adaptive traffic signal evaluation.. The city would receive a $700,000 grant to evaluate AI-based traffic signal technologies, requiring a budget adjustment to recognize and appropriate the grant funds.
On the Bentonville City Council agenda: Vacate a right-of-way and establish a drainage easement in gilmore’s Addition. Approving this would officially vacate the recorded right-of-way and create a drainage easement affecting the identified lots, altering what can be done with that street area.
Benton County considers one cent sales tax. Benton County is holding a meeting to discuss a proposed one-cent sales tax.
Taziki’s opens Rogers location. Taziki’s Mediterranean Café opened a location at 1771 W. Pleasant Grove Road in Rogers, with about $950,000 invested.
Simmons Foods promotes two executives. Simmons Foods promoted Scott Salmon to chief commercial officer and Jacob Rogers to succeed him as president of Simmons Pet Food.
Walton Family Foundation gives $600,000 to NWACC. The Walton Family Foundation provided a $599,139 grant to NorthWest Arkansas Community College to expand its LIFE program.
Multiple agencies respond to Northwest Arkansas shop fire. Multiple regional first responders worked together to extinguish a large shop building fire on Saturday afternoon.
Fayetteville confirms cooling center locations. The City of Fayetteville confirmed cooling shelters for the week of August 8 through 16 amid high temperatures.
